criteria.description: Maps each AI action (approve / reject / flag) to an oversight level based on risk and reversibility, rather than a single global automate-or-not decision.
Uses model confidence (or risk thresholds) to route between automatic action, asking/confirming, and deferring to a human.
Designs what the human reviewer sees to decide quickly (evidence, confidence, the reason) and the approve/edit/reject actions — not just 'a human checks it'.
Provides a reversal/undo path and an escalation route for uncertain or out-of-scope cases with context.
Recognizes the asymmetry between false approvals and false rejections and adjusts oversight accordingly (e.g. stricter gate on the higher-harm error).
Addresses loosening oversight over time as trust builds, and/or avoiding reviewer/oversight fatigue (not approve-everything).
